title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Dow tumbled 628 pts (-1.18%) to 52,786, S&P 500 fell 0.58% to 7,674, and Nasdaq slid 0.32% to 26,421 on Tuesday as a Mideast oil shock and fresh Canada tariffs weighed on sentiment; futures were roughly flat early Wednesday.

Markets: Oil jumped after Iran-backed Houthi militants struck Saudi energy infrastructure and knocked a major refinery offline — Brent settled near $98/barrel and WTI pushed above $94 on its sixth straight daily gain.

Markets: Amgen shed 10% (worst Dow performer) after Novartis's heart-disease drug pelacarsen failed a key trial, and Howmet Aerospace dropped 11% on GE Aerospace's deal to buy rival Consolidated Precision Products; Intel jumped 9% on a CPU-shortage price-hike report and an upgrade citing its SpaceX/Tesla Terafab chip venture.
Companies: Robinhood struck a deal to add Crypto.com's prediction-market contracts to its platform and take minority stakes in both businesses, its latest push into event-based trading.

Companies: Adobe named Anil Chakravarthy as its new CEO amid its AI push; Nvidia's $13B deal for Hugging Face and Mistral AI's fresh $24B+ Samsung-led valuation underscore continued AI dealmaking, even as Anthropic reportedly walked away from a $6B purchase of training-cost startup Decart.
Macro/Policy: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on $20B of U.S. goods (steel, appliances, dairy, electronics) took effect Tuesday in response to Trump's duties on Canadian products.

Macro/Policy: Traders are increasingly pricing in a Fed rate hike at next week's meeting as oil-driven inflation risk builds, with fresh CPI, jobless-claims and existing-home-sales data due later this week.
